note: Read from the FAO's FAOLEX copy of the Children's Act, 1998 (Act 560, assented 30 December 1998); later amendments (among them Act 937 of 2016) weren't read. Majority: section 1, a child is a person below eighteen; held as the age of majority, a reading, since Ghana's age of full capacity was looked for in no other statute. Work: section 89, the minimum age for admission to employment is fifteen; section 90, light work from thirteen (not held); section 91, hazardous work, including work in bars, hotels and places of entertainment where a person may be exposed to immoral behaviour, from eighteen. Performers: the Act names no exception for a child performer, so one under fifteen is held as barred beyond the light work open from thirteen, a reading to check. Service: none. The Government of Ghana's reply to the UN Commission on Human Rights (document E/CN.4/1509, reply dated 23 March 1981): full-time military service in the Ghana Armed Forces is voluntary and Ghana's laws know no conscription or draft. The reply is from 1981; no later text saying otherwise was found (a web search on 2026-10-31 turned up none, and the Ministry of Defence and the Armed Forces' sites reset or failed), so it is held, a reading to check. The National Service Scheme is civilian and not held.

sources.title: UN Digital Library: E/CN.4/1509, Conscientious objection to military service, replies of Governments (Ghana, 23 March 1981)
sources.said: Full time military service in the Ghana Armed Forces is on voluntary basis ... of no conscription or draft.

sources.title: FAOLEX (Food and Agriculture Organization): The Children's Act, 1998 (Act 560) of Ghana
sources.said: Section 1. Definition of child. For purposes of this Act, a child is a person below the age of eighteen ... Section 89. Minimum age for child labour. The minimum age for admission of a child to employment shall be fifteen years. ... Section 90. Minimum age for light work. The minimum age for the engagement of a child in light work shall be thirteen years.
